title: Character computing
summary:
Character computing is a research field that relies on simultaneous development from a computational and psychological perspective and is intended to be used by researchers in both fields. Character computing can be viewed as an extension of the well-established field of affective computing.

Character computing advocates defining behavior as a compound attribute driven not by personality, emotions, situation, or cognition alone, but rather as a function of everything that makes up an individual, their character and the situation they are in. The Character-Behavior-Situation (CBS) triad is at the core of character computing and defines each of the three edges based on the other two.

Character computing as a term was first coined in its first workshop in 2017. Despite its young age, it has already drawn interest in the research community, leading to the publication of the first book under the same title in early 2020 published by Springer Nature. Character computing can be considered as a further extension of both affective computing and personality computing, combining various character states and traits including but not limited to personality and affect.
